S-PRO-1.text: Black screen. Deep space ambient frequencies. Earth appears as a blue marble, then the camera descends rapidly toward the Moon's South Pole.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Narrator
S-PRO-1.text: Three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometers from Earth, there is a place where no trees grow, no wind blows, and no human can take a single breath without life-support.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Narrator
S-PRO-1.text: This is Shackleton Crater. And the lives of four astronauts are in your hands.
The Artemis Lunar Lander touches down on grey lunar regolith. Dust settles.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Leo
S-PRO-1.text: Houston, Shackleton Rim Base here. The First Light has touched down safely.
Leo turns toward the camera, speaking over the direct comm link.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Leo
S-PRO-1.text: Commander, good to have you on the console. I'm Captain Leo Ruiz. These three people beside me are my family now—Amir, Nia, and Daniel.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Leo
S-PRO-1.text: Down here, there is no room for mistakes. If our power dies, our heaters die. If our air tanks run dry, we die. We're counting on your spatial planning and quick thinking to keep us alive.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Amir
S-PRO-1.text: Don't scare the Commander already, Captain! We've got the best tech in the solar system.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Leo
S-PRO-1.text: Technology only works if our Commander connects it right, Amir. Let's get to work.

S-C1-1.speaker: MILO
S-C1-1.text: Unpacking inflatable Crew Habitat. Structural seals engaged.

S-C1-1.speaker: Leo
S-C1-1.text: Commander, anchor that habitat securely. Then we need power to run the air pumps.
Player places Solar Array and connects the power cable.

S-C1-1.speaker: Amir
S-C1-1.text: Power lines connected! Solar wattage is pouring into the main breaker.

S-C1-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C1-1.text: Opening the habitat's compressed oxygen valve. Remember: our air isn't infinite. It comes from high-pressure liquid oxygen tanks delivered with the lander.

S-C1-1.speaker: Nia
S-C1-1.text: We exhale toxic carbon dioxide with every breath. If the CDRA scrubbers aren't powered, CO₂ will poison our blood within hours.
Player powers the CDRA Scrubber and Habitat ventilation.

S-C1-1.speaker: MILO
S-C1-1.text: Cabin atmosphere balanced at 21% O₂, 101.3 kPa.

S-C1-2.text: A shrill alarm echoes through the habitat.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: CRITICAL ALERT: Primary compressed oxygen tank pressure dropping to zero! Valve fracture detected!

S-C1-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C1-2.text: Our reserve oxygen is blowing into the vacuum! We have less than 48 hours of breathable air in the habitat!

S-C1-2.speaker: Leo
S-C1-2.text: Stay calm, team! Panic consumes more oxygen. Commander, open the deep-space transmitter! We need to demand an emergency high-speed cargo resupply from Earth right now!
Player opens the Earth Logistics Menu and clicks Demand Emergency Oxygen Resupply.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: Emergency transmission received by NASA Kennedy Space Center. Rapid-response Falcon Heavy cargo rocket launched with replacement O₂ pods.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: Estimated transit time: 2 Sols. Cabin oxygen reserves are draining.

S-C1-3.text: Player must shed non-vital power, seal interior airlocks, and keep the crew rested to preserve oxygen until the cargo lander thumps down outside.

S-C1-3.speaker: Amir
S-C1-3.text: Cargo lander has touched down! I'm suiting up to haul the new oxygen tanks into the airlock!
Amir replaces the tank. The oxygen gauge surges back to 100%.

S-C1-3.speaker: Leo
S-C1-3.text: Air pressure restored. That was too close, Commander. If that rocket had been delayed by half a day, we wouldn't have survived.

S-C2-1.speaker: MILO
S-C2-1.text: Warning: Orbital sun angle declining. A massive mountain ridge will cast a total shadow over the base for 48 consecutive hours.

S-C2-1.speaker: Amir
S-C2-1.text: Without direct sunlight, our solar panels won't produce a single watt. Outside temperature will plummet to −180 °C.

S-C2-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-1.text: If our electric heaters shut down, the habitat interior will drop below freezing in two hours. Human blood cannot circulate in extreme cold. The crew will freeze to death.

S-C2-1.speaker: Leo
S-C2-1.text: Commander, build high-capacity battery banks immediately. We must store every joule of excess solar power before the shadow arrives.
Player builds Battery Banks and toggles off research labs and floodlights.

S-C2-2.text: Total darkness falls across the base. The base switches to battery power.

S-C2-2.speaker: MILO
S-C2-2.text: Solar generation: 0.0 kW. Battery discharge active.

S-C2-2.speaker: Amir
S-C2-2.text: Captain! The exterior cooling lines on Battery Bank 2 are freezing solid! The battery can't release power when frozen!

S-C2-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-2.text: Cabin temperature is falling fast: 18 °C... 12 °C... 6 °C! We're shivering uncontrollably!

S-C2-2.speaker: Leo
S-C2-2.text: Commander! Reroute the emergency heating loops to the battery core! Do it before our fingers go numb!
Player reroutes the circuit on the thermal panel. Heaters ignite. Temperature stabilizes at 21 °C.

S-C2-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-2.text: Core body temperatures recovering. The heaters saved us.

S-C2-2.speaker: Leo
S-C2-2.text: Good work, Commander. You kept our fire burning in the coldest place in the world.

S-C3-1.text: Nia's science terminal sounds a frantic pulsating siren.

S-C3-1.speaker: Nia
S-C3-1.text: Captain! Look at the NASA DONKI space weather alert! Sunspot 4109 just suffered an X-class solar flare!

S-C3-1.speaker: MILO
S-C3-1.text: A Coronal Mass Ejection is heading directly along the Earth-Moon line. Lethal proton radiation shockwave arrives in 90 minutes.

S-C3-1.speaker: Leo
S-C3-1.text: Standard habitat walls are just thin aluminum and Kevlar. If we stay out here, that radiation will destroy our immune systems and kill us in days.

S-C3-1.speaker: Nia
S-C3-1.text: We need two layers of protection: pile lunar regolith over the roof using the automated rover, and prepare the underground storm bunker surrounded by our water tanks!
Player builds Regolith Shielding and moves crew to the Underground Storm Vault.

S-C3-2.text: Screen shakes violently with static. Radiation monitor outside spikes to 140 mSv/h.

S-C3-2.speaker: MILO
S-C3-2.text: Exterior radiation at lethal levels. Anyone outside would suffer fatal organ failure in 15 minutes.

S-C3-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C3-2.text: Inside the bunker, the water tanks and regolith are absorbing the cosmic rays. Dosimeter reads safe.

S-C3-2.speaker: Leo
S-C3-2.text: Deep breaths, everyone. We wait out the storm together.

S-C4-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C4-1.text: Captain, our packaged rations from Earth are down to their last week. If we don't produce food and water here, starvation will finish us.

S-C4-1.speaker: Nia
S-C4-1.text: Deep inside Shackleton's shadow, there is ancient water ice. If we place an autonomous thermal drill, we can extract pure water.
Player builds Water Extractor and runs power down into the crater.

S-C4-1.speaker: MILO
S-C4-1.text: Water extraction active: +10 L/h of purified liquid water flowing into habitat tanks.

S-C4-2.speaker: Nia
S-C4-2.text: Now we plant the hydroponic lettuce and radishes. They drink our recycled wastewater, absorb the CO₂ we breathe out, and give us fresh calories and pure oxygen.
Player builds Greenhouse Trays. Green sprouts grow.

S-C4-2.speaker: Amir
S-C4-2.text: Look at that! Real green leaves growing in lunar dust! We can actually live here!

S-C4-2.speaker: Leo
S-C4-2.text: Every meal grown here proves that humanity can survive on another world.

S-C5-1.text: The ground quakes violently. Multiple alarm systems scream simultaneously.

S-C5-1.speaker: MILO
S-C5-1.text: 1. Moonquake has severed the main power conduit to Life Support!

S-C5-1.speaker: MILO
S-C5-1.text: 2. Massive electrostatic dust cloud blankets all solar arrays!

S-C5-1.speaker: MILO
S-C5-1.text: 3. Cabin oxygen leaking! Pressure dropping below 70 kPa!

S-C5-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C5-1.text: The oxygen pumps stopped! Leo... Leo went out to manually seal the exterior emergency valve, but his suit radio is breaking up!

S-C5-1.speaker: Leo
S-C5-1.text: (Over crackling static) Commander... the valve is jammed... dust got into the gears... I can't breathe... oxygen running out... you have to... reconnect the power... from your console...

S-C5-1.speaker: Amir
S-C5-1.text: The Captain is dying out there on the surface! We have 60 seconds before he suffocates, and then our own habitat air runs out!

S-C5-2.text: Player executes under intense tension: (1) Toggles emergency batteries directly to the airlock power bus. (2) Cleans the solar panels using automated electrostatic pulse. (3) Reroutes the backup power cable to the primary life-support loop. (4) Presses the emergency repressurization override.

S-C5-2.speaker: MILO
S-C5-2.text: Power circuit restored! Oxygen pressure climbing! Airlock repressurized!
Airlock hisses open. Amir and Daniel drag Captain Leo Ruiz inside, pulling off his helmet. He gasps for air.

S-C5-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C5-2.text: He's breathing! Pulse is returning! Leo, look at me!

S-C5-2.speaker: Leo
S-C5-2.text: (Coughing, then smiling faintly) Good job... Commander. You saved my life... you saved all of us.

S-C5-2.speaker: Amir
S-C5-2.text: We did it! The base held! Everything is green!

S-EPI-1.text: The camera pans through a magnificent, glowing lunar base with greenhouses, batteries, and observation domes. Earth shines brightly overhead.

S-EPI-1.speaker: MILO
S-EPI-1.text: Simulation debrief complete. Survival Rate: 100%. Life-Support Uptime: 98.4%.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: Commander, when we landed, Shackleton Crater was an empty, frozen desert ready to swallow us whole.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: You managed our power, you never let our oxygen run out, you called for help when we needed it, and you kept us alive when disaster struck.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: You aren't just a student anymore. You are a true Mission Commander.
A golden NASA achievement certificate appears on screen (see certificate in story-bible.json).

S-EPI-2.text: M.I.L.O.'s terminal beeps with an encrypted transmission from NASA Deep Space Logistics.

S-EPI-2.speaker: MILO
S-EPI-2.text: Commander, high-priority transmission incoming from Earth.

S-EPI-2.speaker: MILO
S-EPI-2.text: It concerns a new expedition. Target destination: Mars. Distance: 225 million kilometers.
The screen shifts from the silver Moon to a rotating red globe: MARS.

S-EPI-2.speaker: Amir
S-EPI-2.text: Mars? That's going to take a lot of oxygen tanks!

S-EPI-2.speaker: Nia
S-EPI-2.text: Real soil, ancient riverbeds, towering volcanoes... think of the science!

S-EPI-2.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-2.text: Enjoy this victory, Commander. You earned it. But keep your spacesuit ready... Mars is waiting for us.

ambient.speaker: Nia
ambient.text: Look at that horizon! The sun crests over Shackleton, turning the peaks to pure gold.

ambient.speaker: Amir
ambient.text: And more importantly: free solar kilowatts! Time to charge those batteries!

ambient.speaker: Daniel
ambient.text: Captain, our compressed oxygen tank is critically low! We need an Earth resupply before we start seeing stars!

ambient.speaker: Leo
ambient.text: Commander, radio Earth for that cargo rocket! Don't let our air run out!

ambient.speaker: Amir
ambient.text: Direct hit on the landing pad! Fresh oxygen tanks straight from Florida!

ambient.speaker: Amir
ambient.text: Batteries capped at 100%! Ready to face the longest night.

ambient.speaker: Nia
ambient.text: Fresh, crisp lettuce grown right here in lunar gravity. Take that, packaged rations!

ambient.speaker: Leo
ambient.text: Great job, team. A well-fed crew is an invincible crew.

ambient.speaker: Daniel
ambient.text: Everyone inside the water vault! Seal the bulkheads!

ambient.speaker: Leo
ambient.text: Calm and steady. Our Commander has given us the best shields possible.
